Habitat and distribution Soil-dwelling species known from a single locality in eastern Iberian Peninsula (Silvestri 1932 a).

Distribution. China (Guangdong, Henan, Jinlin, Neimeng, Shaanxi, Shenyang, Zhejiang). Comparative diagnosis. This new species is similar to C. proportionis sp. nov., but differs from the latter by having second tergite 0.8 – 0.9 × as long as its apical width, thyridium separated from the basal margin of tergite by its diameter, metasoma not compressed apically, malar space and frons granulose, and metanotum rugose-punctate.

Distribution. This species has a broad range, mostly sympatric with its close ally C. pantherina Stål, from the north of Mexico to the south of Honduras, particularly in the Pacific domain (Fig. 14). The biomes where the species is present are consequently diverse, including the western slopes of the Sierra Madre Occidental Pine-Oak Forests and the Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt, Sierra Madre del Sur, Sierra Madre de Oaxaca and Central American PineOak Forests; Bajío, Balsas, Veracruz, Southern Pacific Dry Forests; and the Petén-Veracruz and Central American Atlantic Moist Forests.
